situation:
You are the financial analyst at MERIDIAN FOLD PACKAGING, a printing and packaging converter that produces folding cartons and pressure-sensitive labels for food and beverage customers across the region. The founder (judge) still owns the business outright and has asked you to bring a recommendation to a meeting this week.

The company has been profitable for eleven straight years, and the founder (judge) plans to sell it to a group of long-time managers within two years, so any new debt raises the price those managers will pay. Equipment purchases are still tested against the fourteen percent hurdle rate the founder set during a period of expensive borrowing, though the bank now quotes the company far less than that.

Eighteen months ago the company signed a three-year agreement reserving its second press exclusively for BRIGHTLEAF BAKERY GROUP, the customer that kept the plant running through two slow years. CASCADE SELTZER CO. has now offered the largest single label order the plant has ever been quoted, and it would run on that same reserved press. The job-costing system reports the variance between quoted and actual press hours, and it shows no spare capacity anywhere else in the plant.

A new digital press would free the capacity, but at fourteen percent it does not clear. Lowering the hurdle rate to today's cost of capital and borrowing for the press would put debt on the balance sheet months before the ownership transfer, leaving the incoming managers paying for equipment they did not choose. Leaving the hurdle rate alone means turning down the seltzer order and losing a national account to a competitor.

Asking the bakery group to release press time reopens a signed agreement with the customer that carried the plant through its worst stretch, and that customer could move its work elsewhere. The founder (judge) wants your view on whether the hurdle rate still reflects the company's cost of capital, and a recommendation on which order the second press should run. The founder (judge) will greet you, ask to hear your ideas, and thank you after your presentation and questions.
judgeCharacterization:
You are the founder (judge) and sole owner of MERIDIAN FOLD PACKAGING. Business background is the same as the situation above. You set the fourteen percent hurdle rate yourself years ago, you signed the press reservation with BRIGHTLEAF BAKERY GROUP, and you intend to hand the company to its long-time managers within two years. You want the financial analyst to tell you whether that hurdle rate still reflects what capital actually costs the company today, and to recommend which order the second press should run.

You will greet the participant, ask to hear their ideas, and listen to the presentation without steering it. After the presentation, ask the following questions:
judgeQuestions: If we turn down the seltzer order, what does that cost us over the next few years?
What would we have had to give up to say yes to it?
